 Multiple flood rescues as heavy rainfall sets in across south-east Queensland
 By Bella Munro
 By Stephen Clarke
 Topic: Weather
 Posted Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 8:29am Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 8:29am Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 8:29am , updated Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 12:22pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 12:22pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 12:22pm Skip to timeline abc.net.au/news/queensland-south-east-storm-warning-live-updates/107294406 Link copied Share Share article Several people have been rescued from floodwaters overnight as heavy rainfall sets in across central and southern Queensland.
 A watch and act prepare to leave warning has been issued for parts of Burpengary and Burpengary East.
 Two public schools and six independent schools have so far announced they will be closed on Friday.
 Keep up with the latest in our live blog.
 Submit a comment or question 
 Log in to comment Live updates
 Pinned Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:16pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:16pm The latest South-East Queensland flooding emergency information
 L By Luke Cooper
 There is a Severe Thunderstorm Warning for heavy rainfall currently issued for South-East Queensland . Here is the latest emergency information:
 As of 11:40am , the warning area is current for potential flash flooding near Cunninghams Gap , Mount Mee and Woodford .
 The slow-moving storm is expected to affect parts of Oakington, Moogerah, Maryvale, Moogerah Dam, Aratula and the   D'Aguilar Ranges over the next hour .
 There is a Prepare to Leave Watch and Act Warning in place for parts of Caboolture and Burpengary , including Beerburrum Rd, Dances Rd, Pumicestone Rd; and Dot Newman Ct in Caboolture .
 The same warning is current for Morayfield Rd and O'Brien Rd in Burpengary , as well as Junction Rd and Childs Dr in Burpengary East .
 There is also a Watch and Act warning to Monitor Conditions for parts of Morayfield , particularly for people around Morayfield Road .
 In the Brisbane City Council area, people are being urged to avoid flooded areas , particularly around Rocklea and Everton Park .
 On the Sunshine Coast , flash flooding is impacting Beerburrum .
 To track the storms on radar and see the storm warning areas, head to the BOM website or app . 
 If you need any emergency assistance , contact the SES on 132 500 .
 If you’re in a life-threatening situation – call Triple Zero . 
 You can also keep listening to ABC Radio or follow along with us here in our live blog - we'll keep you updated with the latest information.

 Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:43pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:43pm Where has the most rain fallen today in SEQ?
 L By Luke Cooper
 While intense rainfall is no longer occurring in parts of South-East Queensland , there are still areas impacted by heavy rain .
 The Bureau of Meteorology tells us that in the hours to 8:30am today:
 163mm of rain was recorded at Mt Reservoir ;
 At least 159mm was recorded at Rose Creek Road in Elimbah ;
 At least 141mm of rain was recorded at Mathew Crescent in Burpengary ;
 At least 168mm of rain was recorded at Sheep Station Creek in Morayfield ;
 At least 159mm of rain was recorded at Short Street in Caboolture .
 A quick check of the latest BOM weather observation totals also shows that to 9am:
 23.6mm of rain fell in Amberley ;
 50.2mm of rain fell in Nambour ;
 24.2mm of rain fell in Beerburrum ;
 22.4mm of rain fell at the Sunshine Coast Airport ;
 15.6mm of rain fell in the Brisbane CBD .
 React React Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:29pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:29pm Locals urged to stay at home
 S By Stephen Clarke
 Prepare to leave alerts are in place for parts of Caboolture, Burpengary and Burpengary East. 
 Moreton Bay Mayor Jodie Shipway has urged locals to stay off the roads.
 "We don't want to put people on the roads unnecessarily to go and get sandbags."
 Mayor Shipway said about 47 local roads in the area have been closed.
 Dozens of roads are closed across multiple suburbs. (ABC News: Janel Shorthouse) React React Key Event
 Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:05pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 1:05pm More than 100 roads closed due to flooding in SEQ
 L By Luke Cooper
 With severe weather continuing to impact South-East Queensland , the state government's Department of Transport and Main Roads has a running list of the roads and highways currently impacted by rising waters.
 This is currently what the TMR's latest closures map looks like:
 (Supplied: QLD TMR) In Greater Brisbane , there are currently 94 road closures due to flooding.
 Those closures include parts of the Mount Lindesay Highway at Park Ridge South , flooding on Morayfield Road and Beerburrum Road in the city's north and Cedar Creek Road at Cedar Creek .
 There are also dozens of smaller, suburban closures in areas across Brisbane's north.
 If you'd like to see the complete list and check the alerts in your local area, you can via the link below:
 Road Condition Information - QLDTraffic 
 React React Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 12:55pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 12:55pm Homeless feeling the impact
 S By Stephen Clarke
 Rough sleepers at Wyllie Park in Moreton Bay were among the first to feel the impact of the heavy rainfall.
 In a statement Moreton Bay Council said it was sending officers out to the park to assess the impact.
 (Supplied: Nourish Street Facebook) "We encourage anyone sleeping rough to move out of low-lying areas or sites near creeks or rivers to safer ground," a spokesperson said.
 Queensland's premier said the flooding was further proof parks should not be places of refuge for the homeless.
 (Supplied: Nourish Street Facebook) "We don't believe that parks are the best place for people to be," the premier said.
 "Parks are for families to go and enjoy themselves"
 His comments come after Economic Development Queensland issued a show cause notice to Moreton Bay City Council over its "illegal" use of the park for the homeless.

 S By Stephen Clarke
 Our own ABC reporter Will Murray was involved in a rescue at Morayfield this morning .
 He swam out with another man after a vehicle stalled in floodwaters and began to sink.
 Will Murray (left) swam out along with another man. (ABC News) React React Key Event

 Morayfield Shopping Centre (Supplied: Eye Envy Optometrist) Multiple roads are closed across south-east Queensland.

 Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 12:24pm Thu 22 Oct 2026 at 12:24pm Recapping the morning
 S By Stephen Clarke
 A severe thunderstorm has hit parts of south-east Queensland causing several flash floods across the region.
 Almost 140mm fell in the three hour period to 7:30am this morning at Caboolture, north of Brisbane.
 Multiple roads across the south-east are flooded.
 Police have responded to rescues from floodwaters and warn residents not to drive through flooded roads.
